articles.text:
Bad Lands Cow Boy,

By A. T. Packard.

Thursday, November 18, 1886.
articles.summary: Page-4 masthead giving the issue date, Thursday, November 18, 1886.

articles.headline: Northern Pacific Time Table.
articles.text:
Northern Pacific Time Table.

WEST BOUND.

Pacific Express, No. 1..........6:45 p. m.
Express Freight, 2d Class..........9:35 p. m.
Freight, 3d Class..........11:40 p. m.

EAST BOUND.

Atlantic Express, No., 2..........8:36 a. m.
Express Freight, 3d Class..........6:20 a. m.

articles.summary: Northern Pacific time table at Medora, D. W. Williams, agent.

articles.text: Northern Pacific preferred stocks, 64½; common, 29⅝.
articles.summary: Northern Pacific stock quotations.

articles.text: Alex. Morton is building an addition to his cottage and making other improvements for winter.
articles.summary: Alex. Morton is enlarging his cottage for winter.

articles.text: R. Nepvne, who has been visiting at the VE horse ranch this summer, started for his home in Holland, last Friday morning.
articles.summary: R. Nepvne left the VE horse ranch for Holland.

articles.text: The cattle-shipping season is nearly ended, but it seems as though there were never more freight trains running than there are at present.
articles.summary: Cattle shipping nearly over but freight traffic heavy.

articles.text: Postals have been sent out to all Billings county's tax-payers, stating the amount of their taxes and conveying a polite intimation that it is time to settle up.
articles.summary: Billings county taxpayers sent tax notices.

articles.text: J. W. Foley who is now here will probably take charge of the Medora interests of the N. P. Ref. Car Co. this winter, W. F. Van Driesche contemplating a trip to Europe.
articles.summary: J. W. Foley likely to take charge of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.'s Medora interests while W. F. Van Driesche goes to Europe.

articles.text: The Maltese Cross, Quarter-circle diamond and KC outfits started on a bull round-up Monday, which will last for several days yet. The object is to gather in the young bulls and weak cows that need feeding.
articles.summary: The Maltese Cross, Quarter-circle diamond and KC outfits began a bull round-up.

articles.text: The school tax for this year in the Medora precinct, is ten mills, which will leave a surplus for next years' expenses. All other taxes for county and territorial purposes, amount to ten and nine-tenths mills.
articles.summary: Medora precinct school tax is ten mills; other taxes 10.9 mills.

articles.text: George W. Fowler, agent and correspondent for the Bismarck Tribune, is in town to-day. The daily Tribune will be sent until March 1 for $2, making it the cheapest and most valuable daily for this part of the country.
articles.summary: Bismarck Tribune agent George W. Fowler is in Medora.

articles.text: Several papers are making mention of remarkable veins of coal in their locality, some going as high as twenty feet. The Bad Lands still takes the lead however in the vein of coal on Deep creek at Mattox' ranch. It is over sixty feet thick in plain sight from the top to the bed of the creek. How much deeper it is no one knows.
articles.summary: A coal vein over sixty feet thick is exposed on Deep creek at Mattox' ranch.

articles.text: The fight over the elections is not ended in Stark county. It will be remembered Trask, according to the returns, had a majority of one over Sebastian. The election was then contested by Mr. Sebastian and it appears with good prospect of succeess, although the courts will be called on to decide the case, no matter how it is decided by the county canvassing board.
articles.summary: Sebastian is contesting Trask's one-vote win in a Stark county election.

articles.text: M. F. Mullins one of the butchers here last summer, won first prize at the recent butchers' contests at the Chicago Fat-Stock show over six other competitors, supposed to be the most skillful in the United States. Mullins' time was ten minutes and seventeen seconds, beating Noonan, another old butcher here, who left in August, by sixteen seconds. Noonan won second prize by twelve seconds.
articles.summary: Former Medora butchers M. F. Mullins and Noonan took first and second prizes at the Chicago Fat-Stock show butchers' contest.

articles.text: Our little flurry of snow three weeks ago, which passed off almost as quickly as it came, was perhaps a harbinger of the disastrous snow storms that have blockaded business in some parts of Indiana, Michigan, New York and eastern states. In many places the snow was from a foot to twenty inches deep on a level, the drifts being from three to ten feet. We doubt if there is now a particle of snow in Dakota and the weather during the day is simply perfect.
articles.summary: Contrasts eastern snowstorms with fine snow-free weather in Dakota.

articles.text:
To close out the stock of Studebaker wagons now on hand, I will make prices for cash that are lower than the wholesale factory rate. The wagons are new and first-class and have Studebaker Bros. full guarantee as to soundness. They will be sold cheaper than any wagons that have ever been sold in this country and cheaper than they can be bought in car lots at the factory. The only reason for making these rates is to close out stock on hand. They must and shall go soon.

A. T. Packard.
articles.summary: Packard offers his Studebaker wagon stock below factory rate to close it out.

articles.text:

Cutler, A — Northrop, W A
Demonde, F B — Pettibone, C J

W. F. Van Driesche, P. M.
articles.summary: List of unclaimed letters at the Medora post office.

articles.headline: NOTICE.
articles.text:
NOTICE.

The co-partnership heretofore existing between the undersigned, is this day dissolved by mutual consent. Martin Timlin will assume all liabilities and all debts due said firm will be paid him. He will continue business at the old stand.

Medora Dak. Nov. 1st. 1886 — M. D. Rider. Martin Timlim.
articles.summary: Notice dissolving the Rider–Timlin partnership; Timlin continues the business (signature printed 'Timlim').

articles.text:
All kinds of wagon extras for sale, including double and single-trees, clevises wrenches, neck-yokes, lock and stay-chains etc.

A. T. Packard.
articles.summary: Packard advertises wagon extras.
